words.enDefinition: Building systems that learn patterns from data to make predictions or find useful structure.

examples.en: The class used machine learning to predict how long different library sorting tasks would take.
examples.zh: 同学们用「机器学习」预测图书馆不同分拣任务需要多长时间。

examples.en: Our first machine learning assignment asked us to group books from their catalogue descriptions.
examples.zh: 我们的第一次「机器学习」作业要求根据目录描述给图书分组。

words.enDefinition: Learning from examples that include known targets for the model to predict.

examples.en: The plant exercise used supervised learning because each training image came with a species label.
examples.zh: 植物练习使用「监督学习」，因为每张训练图像都带有物种标签。

examples.en: We used supervised learning to predict packing times from records that included the actual durations.
examples.zh: 我们使用「监督学习」，根据记录了实际用时的数据预测打包时长。

collocations: train a model with supervised learning

words.enDefinition: Finding patterns or structure in data that has no supplied prediction targets.

examples.en: The team used unsupervised learning to discover groups of books without providing any genre labels.
examples.zh: 团队采用「无监督学习」寻找相近的图书，没有提供任何体裁标签。

examples.en: Our tutor introduced unsupervised learning through an exercise with uncategorised leaf measurements from the garden.
examples.zh: 老师用花园里未经分类的叶片测量数据练习介绍了「无监督学习」。

words.enDefinition: A training approach using both labeled and unlabeled examples for a prediction task.

examples.en: Our exercise used semi-supervised learning because only a few of the plant pictures had labels.
examples.zh: 我们在练习中采用「半监督学习」，因为只有少量植物图片带标签。

examples.en: The tutor asked whether adding the uncategorised books helped the semi-supervised learning approach in this experiment.
examples.zh: 老师问，在这次实验中，加入未分类图书是否改善了「半监督学习」的效果。

collocations: compare semi-supervised learning with supervised learning

words.enDefinition: Examples accompanied by known target values or categories.

examples.en: We used labeled data that paired each book description with a category assigned by the librarian.
examples.zh: 我们使用「有标签数据」，每段图书描述都有一项馆员给出的类别。

examples.en: The class kept part of the labeled data aside to evaluate the plant classifier later.
examples.zh: 同学们留出部分「有标签数据」，供之后评估植物分类器。

words.enDefinition: Examples for which the target values or categories have not been supplied.

examples.en: The exercise used unlabeled data containing leaf measurements gathered before anyone identified the plant species.
examples.zh: 练习所用的「无标签数据」包含识别植物物种之前收集的叶片测量值。

examples.en: We explored the unlabeled data to see which workshop records tended to fall into similar groups.
examples.zh: 我们分析了「无标签数据」，看哪些工作坊记录往往落入相近的组。

words.enDefinition: An individual observation used to fit a model, optionally paired with a target.

examples.en: Each training example recorded the number of books sorted and the time required to sort them.
examples.zh: 每条「训练样本」记录了分拣的图书数量和所需时间。

examples.en: Our tutor removed one training example after discovering that it belonged to the practice test set.
examples.zh: 老师发现其中一条「训练样本」属于练习测试集，于是将其移除。

words.enDefinition: An ordered collection of feature values describing one observation.

examples.en: We made a feature vector for each leaf using its length, width and colour measurements.
examples.zh: 我们用每片叶子的长、宽和色彩测量值创建一个「特征向量」。

examples.en: The tutor checked the feature vector to see whether the two measurements were in the expected order.
examples.zh: 老师检查了「特征向量」，确认两项测量值是否按预计的次序排列。

collocations: represent an observation with a feature vector

words.enDefinition: A table containing the feature values for a collection of observations.

examples.en: The feature matrix had one row per plant and one column per measurement in our exercise.
examples.zh: 练习中的「特征矩阵」每行对应一株植物，每列对应一项测量。

examples.en: We checked the feature matrix before fitting the model to the recorded workshop times.
examples.zh: 在用记录的工作坊用时拟合模型之前，我们先检查了「特征矩阵」。

collocations: fit a model using the feature matrix
inspect the columns of a feature matrix

words.enDefinition: The quantity or category a supervised model is trained to predict.

examples.en: The target variable was the number of minutes needed to finish sorting each batch of books.
examples.zh: 「目标变量」是完成每批图书分拣所需的分钟数。

examples.en: Our tutor asked us to write down the target variable before we selected the input features.
examples.zh: 老师要求我们先写出「目标变量」，再选择输入特征。

words.enDefinition: A value identifying the category assigned to an observation in classification.

examples.en: The librarian assigned a class label to each description based on the book's main subject.
examples.zh: 图书馆员根据图书的主要主题给每段描述分配一个「类别标签」。

examples.en: We compared the predicted class label with the recorded designation for each plant in the exercise.
examples.zh: 对于练习中的每株植物，我们把预测的「类别标签」与已记录的分类作了比较。

words.enDefinition: observed or independently established reference information treated as correct when developing or evaluating a model

examples.en: We used the botanist's labels as ground truth when evaluating the model on the held-out plants.
examples.zh: 评估留出的植物时，我们把植物学家的标签作为「真实标注」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked how uncertain ground truth would affect the findings of the book classification exercise.
examples.zh: 老师问，如果「真实标注」本身不确定，会怎样影响图书分类练习的结论。

collocations: use expert labels as ground truth

words.enDefinition: Predicting a category or a set of categories for an observation.

examples.en: The classification exercise assigned each book to one of the library's four broad subject categories.
examples.zh: 「分类」练习把每本书分到图书馆四大主题类别之一。

examples.en: We used classification to predict whether a photographed leaf belonged to one of the target species.
examples.zh: 我们用「分类」预测照片中的叶片是否属于目标物种之一。

words.enDefinition: Predicting a numerical target, such as a measurement or duration, from input values.

examples.en: The regression exercise predicted the number of minutes needed to complete a classroom sorting activity.
examples.zh: 「回归」练习预测完成一项课堂分拣活动需要的分钟数。

examples.en: We chose regression because the target was a temperature measurement rather than a named category.
examples.zh: 目标是温度测量值，因此我们选择了「回归」。

words.enDefinition: Grouping similar observations by their features without using supplied category labels.

examples.en: We used clustering to see which leaf measurements formed natural groups in the practice dataset.
examples.zh: 我们用「聚类」看看练习数据集中的哪些叶片测量值能自然地分成一组。

examples.en: The library exercise used clustering to find similar descriptions before anyone gave the groups names.
examples.zh: 图书馆练习在尚未给各组取名时使用「聚类」寻找相近的描述。

words.enDefinition: A classification task with exactly two possible categories.

examples.en: The library used binary classification to distinguish books for young readers from the other books.
examples.zh: 图书馆用「二分类」区分供低龄读者阅读的图书与其他图书。

examples.en: Our worksheet introduced binary classification with two possible outcomes for each photographed garden leaf.
examples.zh: 练习表用每张花园叶片照片的两种可能结果来介绍「二分类」。

collocations: use binary classification for two categories

words.enDefinition: Assigning one category to each example from more than two mutually exclusive categories.

examples.en: The team used multiclass classification to assign each sample to one of four plant species.
examples.zh: 团队用「多类别分类」将每个样本归到四种植物中的一种。

examples.en: Our tutor used multiclass classification when each book could have only one of five catalogue labels.
examples.zh: 每本书只能有五种编目标签之一时，老师用了「多类别分类」。

words.enDefinition: A task that can assign several labels to the same example.

examples.en: We used multilabel classification because each classroom document could cover both science and local history.
examples.zh: 我们用「多标签分类」，因为一份课堂文档可能同时涉及科学和地方历史。

examples.en: Our tutor contrasted multilabel classification with assigning only one catalogue label to every book.
examples.zh: 老师把「多标签分类」与为每本书只分配一个编目标签的做法作了比较。

words.enDefinition: The category chosen as the event of interest in binary classification.

examples.en: The worksheet treated oak leaves as the positive class because those were the examples we wanted to find.
examples.zh: 练习表将橡树叶作为「正类」，因为它们是我们要找的样本。

examples.en: We had to state the positive class before explaining the errors made by our classifier.
examples.zh: 解释分类器的错误之前，我们必须先说明哪个类别是「正类」。

collocations: count examples in the positive class

words.enDefinition: The other category in binary classification, outside the chosen event of interest.

examples.en: The negative class contained all the garden leaves that were not from oak trees.
examples.zh: 「负类」包含花园里所有非橡树的叶片。

examples.en: The tutor asked why the model assigned this particular leaf to the negative class.
examples.zh: 老师问，模型为什么把这片叶子分到了「负类」。

collocations: count examples in the negative class

words.enDefinition: A target measured on a continuous numerical scale.

examples.en: The example used elapsed time as a continuous target and rounded it only for the report.
examples.zh: 例题把实际用时作为「连续型目标」，只在写报告时对它取整。

examples.en: The tutor asked us to identify the continuous target among the three outcomes listed in the exercise.
examples.zh: 老师让我们在练习列出的三个结果中找出「连续型目标」。

collocations: evaluate predictions for a continuous target

words.enDefinition: The category a fitted classifier assigns to a particular example.

examples.en: The report listed the predicted class beside the librarian's label for each book in the exercise.
examples.zh: 报告把每本练习用书的「预测类别」列在馆员所给标签旁边。

examples.en: We checked the predicted class for a leaf whose shape resembled those of two species.
examples.zh: 我们检查了那片外形与两种植物叶片都相像的叶片的「预测类别」。

collocations: compare the predicted class with the true class

words.enDefinition: A model's estimate of how likely a specified class or event is for an example.

examples.en: The model assigned a predicted probability of eighty percent to the oak label for this leaf.
examples.zh: 模型预测这片叶子属于橡树叶的「预测概率」为百分之八十。

examples.en: Our group compared the predicted probability with the outcome observed for each group of similar cases.
examples.zh: 我们组把「预测概率」和每组相似样本中观察到的结果作了比较。

words.enDefinition: A boundary in feature space separating regions where a classifier predicts different classes.

examples.en: The diagram showed the decision boundary between plant categories using leaf length and width.
examples.zh: 图中利用叶片长度和宽度展示了植物类别之间的「决策边界」。

examples.en: We noticed that the decision boundary moved after the model saw additional training examples.
examples.zh: 我们注意到，模型加入额外训练样本后，「决策边界」发生了移动。

collocations: learn a decision boundary from data

words.enDefinition: The probability cutoff used to make a classification decision.

examples.en: We lowered the probability threshold and the classifier marked more pictures as containing oak leaves.
examples.zh: 我们调低「概率阈值」后，分类器把更多图片标为含有橡树叶。

examples.en: The tutor asked us to choose a probability threshold using the validation results from the exercise.
examples.zh: 老师要求我们根据练习的验证结果选择一个「概率阈值」。

collocations: compare results at different probability thresholds

words.enDefinition: Modeling a numerical outcome as a weighted sum of input features, often with an intercept.

examples.en: We used linear regression to predict sorting time from the number of books in each batch.
examples.zh: 我们用「线性回归」根据每批图书的数量预测分拣用时。

examples.en: Our tutor compared linear regression with a more flexible model on the same set of records.
examples.zh: 老师用同一组记录比较了「线性回归」和更灵活的模型。

collocations: evaluate the fit of linear regression

words.enDefinition: a model for class probabilities using logistic or related links applied to scores that are linear in the input features

examples.en: The workshop used logistic regression to estimate whether an image showed an oak leaf or another leaf.
examples.zh: 工作坊用「逻辑回归」估计图像显示的是橡树叶还是其他叶片。

examples.en: Our tutor used logistic regression to show how a classifier can return estimated probabilities.
examples.zh: 老师用「逻辑回归」说明分类器怎样返回估计概率。

words.enDefinition: A classifier that follows a series of feature tests from a root to a prediction leaf.

examples.en: The decision tree classifier checked leaf shape first and then considered the length measurement.
examples.zh: 「决策树分类器」先检查叶形，再考虑测得的长度。

examples.en: We followed the decision tree classifier from its first question to the predicted library category.
examples.zh: 我们沿着「决策树分类器」从第一个判断一直走到预测的图书类别。

collocations: limit the depth of a decision tree classifier

words.enDefinition: An ensemble of randomized decision trees whose outputs are combined for prediction.

examples.en: The random forest combined predictions from several trees to categorise the sample book descriptions.
examples.zh: 「随机森林」汇总了多棵树的预测，对示例图书描述进行归类。

examples.en: Our group compared a random forest with a single tree on the same validation data.
examples.zh: 我们组在同一批验证数据上比较了「随机森林」和单棵决策树。

collocations: adjust the size of a random forest

words.enDefinition: A classifier predicting from the labels of nearby training examples under a chosen similarity or distance measure.

examples.en: The nearest-neighbor classifier compared each new leaf with similar leaves that already had known labels.
examples.zh: 「最近邻分类器」将每片新叶子与标签已知的相似叶片作比较。

examples.en: Our tutor asked how the nearest-neighbor classifier would behave if different measurements used very different scales.
examples.zh: 老师问，如果各项测量的取值尺度差异很大，「最近邻分类器」的表现会怎样。

collocations: change the settings of a nearest-neighbor classifier

words.enDefinition: partitioning observations into a specified number of clusters by seeking to reduce the sum of squared distances to their assigned centres

examples.en: We used k-means clustering to group leaves by length and width without giving the groups names.
examples.zh: 我们用「K 均值聚类」按叶片长宽分组，未给这些组命名。

examples.en: The tutor repeated k-means clustering with another starting configuration to compare the resulting groups.
examples.zh: 老师更换初始配置再做一次「K 均值聚类」，以比较得到的分组。

collocations: choose the cluster count for k-means clustering

words.enDefinition: In k-means, the mean feature vector of the observations assigned to a cluster.

examples.en: The cluster centroid represented the average measurements for the leaves assigned to the first group.
examples.zh: 「簇质心」表示分到第一组的叶片的平均测量值。

examples.en: We recalculated the cluster centroid after two samples moved to a different group in the example.
examples.zh: 例题中两个样本移至另一组之后，我们重新计算了「簇质心」。

collocations: measure distance to a cluster centroid

words.enDefinition: Building nested groups of observations by successively merging or splitting them.

examples.en: We used hierarchical clustering to see which book groups combined as the similarity requirement changed.
examples.zh: 我们用「层次聚类」观察相似程度要求变化后，哪些图书分组会合并。

examples.en: Our tutor drew the nested groups produced by hierarchical clustering in the practice exercise.
examples.zh: 老师画出了练习中「层次聚类」得到的嵌套分组。

collocations: inspect the result of hierarchical clustering

words.enDefinition: Representing observations with fewer dimensions while retaining useful information from the original features.

examples.en: The team used dimensionality reduction to represent many leaf measurements with a smaller set of values.
examples.zh: 团队用「降维」将多项叶片测量值表示成一组较少的值。

examples.en: Our tutor asked which information was lost during dimensionality reduction in the book description exercise.
examples.zh: 老师问，在图书描述练习的「降维」过程中丢失了哪些信息。

words.enDefinition: A linear transformation that finds orthogonal directions ordered by the variance they explain.

examples.en: We used principal component analysis to summarise several related leaf measurements before exploring the sample groups.
examples.zh: 探索样本分组前，我们用「主成分分析」概括几项相关的叶片测量值。

examples.en: The lab used principal component analysis to see how much variation the first two components captured.
examples.zh: 实验用「主成分分析」查看前两个成分能解释多少变异。

collocations: fit principal component analysis on training data
choose components for principal component analysis

words.enDefinition: To estimate a model's learned settings from training data.

examples.en: We needed to fit a model before predicting the time required for the next sorting task.
examples.zh: 预测下一项分拣任务的用时之前，我们需要先「拟合模型」。

examples.en: The tutor asked us to fit a model using only the records from our training set.
examples.zh: 老师要求我们仅使用训练集中的记录来「拟合模型」。

collocations: fit a model to the data
fit a model on the training set
fit a model with fewer features

words.enDefinition: Using a trained model to produce outputs for supplied inputs.

examples.en: The app ran model inference when we presented a new leaf photograph during the demonstration.
examples.zh: 演示中，我们给应用一张新的叶片照片时，它执行了「模型推理」。

examples.en: Our report timed model inference separately from the work of fitting the classifier in class.
examples.zh: 报告分别计量了「模型推理」与课堂上拟合分类器的耗时。

collocations: perform model inference on new data

words.enDefinition: Values learned during fitting that determine how a model produces its outputs.

examples.en: The model parameters changed when the regression was fitted to the larger set of workshop records.
examples.zh: 用更大的一组工作坊记录拟合回归模型后，「模型参数」发生了变化。

examples.en: We compared the model parameters to see how two features contributed to the predicted times.
examples.zh: 我们比较了「模型参数」，看两个特征分别怎样影响用时预测。

words.enDefinition: A setting of a model or training procedure chosen outside the fitting of its learned parameters.

examples.en: The tutor described tree depth as a hyperparameter we could restrict before fitting the model.
examples.zh: 老师介绍，树的最大深度是一项可在模型拟合前限制的「超参数」。

examples.en: We changed one hyperparameter at a time while comparing results on the same validation examples.
examples.zh: 在同一组验证样本上对比结果时，我们每次只改一个「超参数」。

collocations: choose a value for a hyperparameter

words.enDefinition: A function that measures prediction error or penalty given the model's outputs and the observed targets.

examples.en: The loss function gave a larger penalty to predictions that differed greatly from the recorded times.
examples.zh: 「损失函数」对与记录用时相差较大的预测施加了更大的惩罚。

examples.en: We compared two models after using the same loss function to evaluate their sorting time predictions.
examples.zh: 我们用同一个「损失函数」评估两种模型对分拣用时的预测后，再比较模型。

collocations: evaluate the loss function on predictions

words.enDefinition: Loss evaluated on observations used to fit the model.

examples.en: The training loss dropped as the model's predicted sorting times approached the recorded training values.
examples.zh: 随着模型预测的分拣时间接近训练数据中的实测用时，「训练损失」下降了。

examples.en: Our report listed training loss separately from errors measured on the held-out examples.
examples.zh: 报告把「训练损失」与在留出样本上测得的误差分开列出。

words.enDefinition: Loss evaluated on data reserved for comparing models or training choices.

examples.en: The validation loss started rising even though the model kept improving on the original training examples.
examples.zh: 尽管模型在原训练样本上的表现持续改善，「验证损失」却开始上升。

examples.en: We recorded validation loss after every full pass through the training data in our experiment.
examples.zh: 实验中，每完整遍历一次训练数据，我们就记录一次「验证损失」。

collocations: choose an epoch based on validation loss

words.enDefinition: An iterative optimization method that updates parameters in the direction opposite the gradient of the objective.

examples.en: The exercise used gradient descent to adjust the line until predicted sorting times improved on average.
examples.zh: 练习用「梯度下降」调整直线，使分拣用时的预测整体有所改善。

examples.en: Our tutor drew two steps of gradient descent on a simple curve representing the loss.
examples.zh: 老师在表示损失的一条简单曲线上画出了「梯度下降」的两个步骤。

words.enDefinition: A training setting controlling the size of parameter updates in methods such as gradient descent.

examples.en: A smaller learning rate made each update to the model's weights less pronounced.
examples.zh: 较小的「学习率」让模型权重每次更新的幅度减小。

examples.en: We changed the learning rate after seeing the sample model jump past the lowest point repeatedly.
examples.zh: 看到示例模型反复跳过最低点后，我们调整了「学习率」。

words.enDefinition: One full pass through the training examples during a fitting procedure.

examples.en: The report showed the classifier's loss after each training epoch in the leaf recognition exercise.
examples.zh: 报告展示了叶片识别练习中每个「训练轮次」之后分类器的损失。

examples.en: One training epoch took longer after we added more book descriptions to the practice dataset.
examples.zh: 把更多图书描述加入练习数据集后，一个「训练轮次」用时更长了。

collocations: evaluate the model after a training epoch

words.enDefinition: A small subset of training examples processed together for a training update.

examples.en: Each mini-batch contained a few photographs whose prediction errors contributed to the next update.
examples.zh: 每个「小批量」含有几张照片，对应的预测误差会参与下一次更新。

examples.en: Our tutor compared using a mini-batch with processing the entire training set for every update.
examples.zh: 老师对比了每次更新时使用一个「小批量」和处理整个训练集的做法。

collocations: compute the loss for a mini-batch

words.enDefinition: Ending training when a monitored criterion suggests further fitting is unlikely to improve the model.

examples.en: We used early stopping after the validation loss stopped improving across several rounds of training.
examples.zh: 验证损失连续几轮未改善后，我们采用了「提前停止」。

examples.en: The tutor compared early stopping with letting the classroom experiment continue for the full planned duration.
examples.zh: 老师对比了「提前停止」和让课堂实验跑完全部预定时长的做法。

collocations: monitor validation loss for early stopping

words.enDefinition: Constraining a model or its fitting to limit excessive flexibility and improve generalization.

examples.en: We applied regularization to keep the regression coefficients small in the sorting time exercise.
examples.zh: 我们在分拣用时练习中应用「正则化」，限制回归系数的大小。

examples.en: Our tutor compared regularization settings after finding that the flexible model had fitted the training noise.
examples.zh: 老师发现灵活模型拟合了训练噪声后，对比了几种「正则化」设置。

words.enDefinition: The setting that controls how strongly fitting penalizes or restricts model complexity.

examples.en: We varied regularization strength to see which setting worked best on held-out plant examples.
examples.zh: 我们改变「正则化强度」，查看哪个设置在留出的植物样本上效果最好。

examples.en: The tutor increased regularization strength in the example and showed how its coefficients changed.
examples.zh: 老师提高例题的「正则化强度」，展示模型系数随之怎样变化。

words.enDefinition: A regularization term proportional to the sum of the absolute magnitudes of selected parameters.

examples.en: The regression example used an L1 penalty and several coefficients became exactly zero during fitting.
examples.zh: 回归例题采用了「L1 惩罚项」，拟合过程中有几个系数变为零。

examples.en: We compared validation errors after adding an L1 penalty to the book handling time predictor.
examples.zh: 我们给图书处理用时预测模型加上「L1 惩罚项」，然后比较验证误差。

collocations: fit a model with an L1 penalty
choose the weight of an L1 penalty

words.enDefinition: A regularization term proportional to the sum of squares of selected model parameters.

examples.en: The example applied an L2 penalty to discourage large coefficients in its linear regression model.
examples.zh: 例题用「L2 惩罚项」约束线性回归模型中的较大系数。

examples.en: Our tutor compared the fitted coefficients before and after introducing an L2 penalty.
examples.zh: 老师对比了引入「L2 惩罚项」前后的拟合系数。

collocations: fit a model with an L2 penalty
choose the weight of an L2 penalty

words.enDefinition: How flexible a model is in the patterns it can represent.

examples.en: We increased model complexity by letting the practice tree ask more questions before predicting a category.
examples.zh: 我们允许练习决策树在预测类别前提出更多判断问题，提高了「模型复杂度」。

examples.en: The tutor discussed model complexity while comparing a straight line with a much more flexible curve.
examples.zh: 老师将直线与更灵活的曲线作对比时，讨论了「模型复杂度」。

words.enDefinition: Learning details specific to the training data that do not transfer well to unseen examples.

examples.en: The team suspected overfitting because the model predicted familiar leaves well but struggled with new ones.
examples.zh: 模型很擅长预测熟悉的叶片，却难以判断新叶片，因此团队怀疑存在「过拟合」。

examples.en: Our tutor compared scores on training and validation examples when discussing possible overfitting in the experiment.
examples.zh: 老师讨论实验中可能的「过拟合」时，比较了训练样本和验证样本上的得分。

words.enDefinition: Failure to learn important patterns, often leading to poor results even on the training data.

examples.en: The straight-line model showed underfitting because the training relationship curved sharply across the observed sorting times.
examples.zh: 训练数据中的分拣用时关系明显弯曲，因此直线模型表现出「欠拟合」。

examples.en: Our report discussed underfitting after the simplified model performed poorly on both training and validation examples.
examples.zh: 过于简单的模型在训练和验证样本上表现都很差，我们在报告里讨论了「欠拟合」。

words.enDefinition: The ability of a learned model to perform well on examples outside its training data.

examples.en: We assessed generalization by testing the leaf classifier on samples from plants it had never seen.
examples.zh: 我们用分类器没见过的植物样本做测试，评估它的「泛化」能力。

examples.en: Our tutor discussed generalization after checking whether the new book descriptions resembled the original training examples.
examples.zh: 老师查看新的图书描述是否与原训练样本相近以后，讨论了「泛化」。

words.enDefinition: The difference between performance on the training data and performance on unseen data.

examples.en: The generalization gap grew when the classifier improved on training photographs but lost accuracy on new ones.
examples.zh: 分类器在训练照片上进步、在新照片上的准确率下降时，「泛化差距」扩大了。

examples.en: We compared the generalization gap for two models fitted to the same set of garden measurements.
examples.zh: 我们比较了用同一组花园测量数据拟合的两种模型的「泛化差距」。

collocations: report a generalization gap between scores

words.enDefinition: The balance between systematic prediction error and sensitivity to variations in the training sample.

examples.en: Our tutor explained the bias-variance trade-off by comparing a rigid line with a highly flexible curve.
examples.zh: 老师用一条刚性的直线和一条非常灵活的曲线作对比，解释了「偏差与方差的权衡」。

examples.en: We used repeated fits of the time predictor to illustrate the bias-variance trade-off in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们多次拟合用时预测模型，以说明「偏差与方差的权衡」。

collocations: illustrate the bias-variance trade-off with two models

words.enDefinition: In bias–variance analysis, the difference between a model's average prediction and the underlying target function.

examples.en: The simulation showed model bias because the average fitted line missed the curve that generated the data.
examples.zh: 模拟中，平均拟合线偏离了生成数据的曲线，体现了「模型偏差」。

examples.en: Our tutor used a known target function to show how model bias could be estimated.
examples.zh: 老师用一个已知的目标函数展示了怎样估计「模型偏差」。

collocations: explain model bias with a known target function

words.enDefinition: Variation in a model's predictions across different training samples drawn under comparable conditions.

examples.en: The simulation showed high model variance when small changes in the sample produced very different fitted curves.
examples.zh: 样本稍有变化就得到差异很大的拟合曲线，模拟因此显示较高的「模型方差」。

examples.en: We compared model variance by examining the predictions from several independent training samples in the exercise.
examples.zh: 我们查看了用练习中几个独立训练样本拟合后得到的预测，比较「模型方差」。

collocations: illustrate model variance across training samples

words.enDefinition: Prediction error that remains even for the best possible predictor given the available information.

examples.en: The simulation included irreducible error because equally sized book batches could take different amounts of time.
examples.zh: 模拟加入了「不可约误差」，因为相同大小的图书批次实际用时也可能不同。

examples.en: Our tutor explained why a more flexible model could not remove the irreducible error in the simulation.
examples.zh: 老师解释了为何更灵活的模型仍无法消除模拟中的「不可约误差」。

collocations: distinguish irreducible error from model error
estimate irreducible error in a simulation

words.enDefinition: Prediction error on observations that were not used to fit the model.

examples.en: We estimated out-of-sample error by testing the time predictor on a fresh set of workshop records.
examples.zh: 我们用一组新的工作坊记录测试用时预测模型，以估计「样本外误差」。

examples.en: The tutor compared the out-of-sample error with the error the model recorded during training.
examples.zh: 老师比较了「样本外误差」与模型在训练期间记录的误差。

collocations: report out-of-sample error on held-out data

words.enDefinition: Information reaching training or model selection that would be unavailable when evaluating or using the model in its intended setting.

examples.en: We identified data leakage after finding the same photographed leaf on both sides of the split.
examples.zh: 发现拆分后的两边都含有同一片叶片的照片后，我们识别出了「数据泄漏」。

examples.en: The worksheet showed how fitting a transformation on all examples could introduce data leakage before evaluation.
examples.zh: 练习表展示了用所有样本拟合数据变换怎样在评估前引入「数据泄漏」。

collocations: detect data leakage between training and test data

words.enDefinition: Use of a feature that reveals the outcome through information unavailable at prediction time.

examples.en: The tutor found target leakage because the predictor used a completion note written after the task ended.
examples.zh: 老师发现了「目标泄漏」，因为预测模型用了任务结束后才写下的完成记录。

examples.en: We removed a column that directly encoded the final category after identifying target leakage in the exercise.
examples.zh: 在练习中识别出「目标泄漏」后，我们移除了直接编码最终类别的一列。

collocations: remove a feature causing target leakage

words.enDefinition: In model evaluation, a plot of training and validation performance against the amount of training data.

examples.en: The learning curve showed whether the leaf classifier improved as we added more training examples.
examples.zh: 「学习曲线」展示了增加训练样本后，叶片分类器是否有所改善。

examples.en: Our tutor used a learning curve to compare performance at four different training sample sizes.
examples.zh: 老师用「学习曲线」比较四种训练样本数量下的模型表现。

collocations: compare learning curves for two models

words.enDefinition: A measure of how strongly a feature contributes to predictions under a specified assessment method.

examples.en: We checked feature importance to see how much leaf width contributed to the classifier under our chosen method.
examples.zh: 我们检查了「特征重要性」，看看按所选方法衡量，叶宽对分类器的贡献有多大。

examples.en: Our tutor cautioned that feature importance alone could not tell us which measurements caused a plant's label.
examples.zh: 老师提醒，仅凭「特征重要性」无法判断哪些测量值是植物被标为某类的原因。

words.enDefinition: the alignment of predicted probabilities with observed event frequencies, or the process of improving that alignment

examples.en: We checked probability calibration by comparing the average predicted probability with the observed frequency within each group.
examples.zh: 我们比较了每组的平均预测概率与实际观测频率，以检查「概率校准」情况。

examples.en: Our tutor used probability calibration to discuss whether predictions of eighty percent were consistent with observed outcomes.
examples.zh: 老师用「概率校准」讨论预测概率为百分之八十的结果是否与实际情况一致。

collocations: check probability calibration on held-out data

words.enDefinition: A change in how data or outcomes are distributed between training and later use or evaluation.

examples.en: The team suspected distribution shift because the new leaf photographs were taken under very different lighting.
examples.zh: 新叶片照片的光照条件差异很大，团队怀疑出现了「分布偏移」。

examples.en: We discussed distribution shift after finding that the new library featured many book genres absent from training.
examples.zh: 发现新图书馆中有不少训练时没有见过的图书体裁后，我们讨论了「分布偏移」。

collocations: evaluate a model under distribution shift

words.enDefinition: The observed numerical outcome minus the model's fitted value for that example.

examples.en: The prediction residual was positive because the sorting task took longer than the model had predicted.
examples.zh: 分拣任务实际用时比模型预测的长，所以「预测残差」为正。

examples.en: We inspected each prediction residual before deciding whether larger batches were systematically taking longer than predicted.
examples.zh: 在判断较大批次是不是普遍比预测用时更长之前，我们逐条检查了「预测残差」。

collocations: inspect prediction residuals for a pattern
compare the sign of each prediction residual

words.enDefinition: The portion of a dataset used to fit a model's learned parameters.

examples.en: We used the training set to fit a model that predicted sorting times for book batches.
examples.zh: 我们用「训练集」拟合一个预测每批图书分拣用时的模型。

examples.en: The training set contained photographs from six different garden beds in our classroom exercise.
examples.zh: 课堂练习的「训练集」含有六块不同花坛的照片。

collocations: reserve examples outside the training set

words.enDefinition: A set of examples used to compare models or choose settings during development.

examples.en: We used the validation set to choose how deep the book classification tree should grow.
examples.zh: 我们用「验证集」决定图书分类树应当长到多深。

examples.en: The tutor asked us to compare both models on the same validation set before choosing one.
examples.zh: 老师要求我们选模型前先在同一个「验证集」上比较这两个模型。

collocations: evaluate models on a validation set

words.enDefinition: A set of examples reserved for assessing a model after development and selection are complete.

examples.en: We left the test set untouched until the library classification model and its settings were settled.
examples.zh: 我们保持「测试集」未被使用，直到图书馆分类模型及其设置确定下来。

examples.en: The report gave the accuracy on the test set after selecting the final leaf classifier.
examples.zh: 选定最终的叶片分类器后，报告给出了模型在「测试集」上的准确率。

words.enDefinition: Partitioning observations into separate portions for fitting and final evaluation.

examples.en: We made a train-test split before fitting the model to the workshop completion records.
examples.zh: 我们先进行了「训练与测试拆分」，才用工作坊完成记录拟合模型。

examples.en: Our tutor checked the train-test split to verify that no plant appeared in both portions.
examples.zh: 老师检查「训练与测试拆分」，确认没有任何一株植物同时出现在两部分。

collocations: check a train-test split for overlap
use the same train-test split for comparisons

words.enDefinition: Evaluating a model on a reserved portion of the data after fitting on the remaining portion.

examples.en: The exercise used holdout validation by reserving one fixed portion of the workshop records for evaluation.
examples.zh: 练习保留了工作坊记录的固定一部分做评估，采用的是「留出法验证」。

examples.en: We chose holdout validation so every trial model could be compared on the same reserved examples.
examples.zh: 我们选择「留出法验证」，以便让每个试验模型在相同的留出样本上比较。

words.enDefinition: Evaluating a learning procedure by repeatedly fitting and validating on different data partitions.

examples.en: We used cross-validation to compare two plant classifiers without relying on a single fixed partition.
examples.zh: 我们用「交叉验证」比较两个植物分类器，无需依赖单一的固定划分。

examples.en: The tutor showed how cross-validation let different examples serve as validation data in different rounds.
examples.zh: 老师演示了「交叉验证」怎样在不同轮次使用不同样本作为验证数据。

words.enDefinition: Dividing data into k folds and validating each fold once after fitting on the remaining folds.

examples.en: We used k-fold cross-validation so each part of the practice dataset was held out once.
examples.zh: 我们使用「K 折交叉验证」，让练习数据集的每个部分都被留出一次。

examples.en: Our tutor drew five partitions to illustrate k-fold cross-validation for the library exercise.
examples.zh: 老师画出五个分区，说明图书馆练习中的「K 折交叉验证」。

words.enDefinition: The subset held out for evaluation in one round of a cross-validation procedure.

examples.en: The model was scored on a different validation fold during each round of our exercise.
examples.zh: 练习的每一轮都在不同的「验证折」上对模型打分。

examples.en: We wrote down which plants belonged to the current validation fold before fitting the next model.
examples.zh: 拟合下一个模型前，我们写下了当前「验证折」包含哪些植物。

collocations: score a model on a validation fold

words.enDefinition: A partition designed to preserve class proportions approximately across the resulting subsets.

examples.en: We used a stratified split so the rarer plant species still appeared in both portions.
examples.zh: 我们用「分层拆分」，使较少见的植物物种在两部分都仍有样本。

examples.en: Our tutor inspected class counts after the stratified split to confirm the proportions were similar.
examples.zh: 老师在「分层拆分」之后检查各类别的数量，以确认比例接近。

collocations: preserve class proportions with a stratified split
compare a stratified split with an ordinary split

words.zhGloss: 分层 K 折交叉验证
words.enDefinition: K-fold validation that aims to keep class proportions similar in each fold.
acceptedZhAnswers: 分层 K 折交叉验证

examples.en: We used stratified k-fold cross-validation because the sample contained far fewer oak leaves than other leaves.
examples.zh: 样本中的橡树叶远少于其他叶片，因此我们使用了「分层 K 折交叉验证」。

examples.en: Our tutor checked whether stratified k-fold cross-validation kept each class represented across the practice folds.
examples.zh: 老师核查了「分层 K 折交叉验证」是否让各类别在各折中都得到覆盖。

collocations: choose a fold count for stratified k-fold cross-validation
inspect class coverage under stratified k-fold cross-validation

words.enDefinition: Cross-validation that keeps related observations from the same group together when separating training and validation data.

examples.en: We used grouped cross-validation because several photographs came from each plant in the garden exercise.
examples.zh: 我们用了「分组交叉验证」，因为花园练习中每株植物可能有多张照片。

examples.en: Our tutor checked that grouped cross-validation kept photos of each plant together in every round.
examples.zh: 老师核查了「分组交叉验证」是否在每一轮都把同一株植物的照片放在一起。

words.enDefinition: Cross-validation that holds out one observation at a time and fits on all the others.

examples.en: We used leave-one-out cross-validation for the tiny workshop dataset containing only eight completed tasks.
examples.zh: 这个很小的工作坊数据集只有八项已完成任务，我们用的是「留一交叉验证」。

examples.en: Our worksheet illustrated leave-one-out cross-validation by moving a single record into the reserved portion each round.
examples.zh: 练习表每轮放一条记录到留出部分，以说明「留一交叉验证」。

collocations: score a model with leave-one-out cross-validation
compare leave-one-out cross-validation with larger folds

words.enDefinition: Cross-validation with inner splits for tuning and separate outer splits for estimating the tuned procedure's performance.

examples.en: The assignment used nested cross-validation to separate choosing tree settings from estimating the resulting model's performance.
examples.zh: 作业使用「嵌套交叉验证」，把选择树的设置与估计所得模型的表现分开。

examples.en: We marked the inner and outer folds before running nested cross-validation on the practice records.
examples.zh: 我们先标出内层和外层各折，再在练习记录上跑「嵌套交叉验证」。

collocations: report outer scores from nested cross-validation

words.enDefinition: A partition that respects the time order, training on earlier observations and evaluating on later ones.

examples.en: We used a time-series split so the model trained on earlier weeks and predicted later ones.
examples.zh: 我们用「时间序列拆分」，让模型在较早几周的数据上训练，再预测之后几周。

examples.en: The tutor checked the dates in the time-series split before we compared the forecast errors.
examples.zh: 老师核对了「时间序列拆分」中的日期，我们随后比较预测误差。

collocations: use a time-series split for evaluation
check the dates in a time-series split

words.enDefinition: Repeatedly drawing samples with replacement from the available observations.

examples.en: We used bootstrap resampling to compare model predictions across varied samples of the same workshop records.
examples.zh: 我们用「自助法重采样」，比较模型在同一组工作坊记录的不同重抽样本下的预测。

examples.en: The tutor used bootstrap resampling to show why some practice observations appeared more than once.
examples.zh: 老师用「自助法重采样」说明为什么某些练习观测值会出现不止一次。

collocations: generate new samples with bootstrap resampling

words.enDefinition: a performance estimate obtained from ensemble members that left each evaluated observation out of their bootstrap sample

examples.en: The model report listed an out-of-bag score for the forest fitted to the sample leaf measurements.
examples.zh: 模型报告列出了根据示例叶片测量值拟合的森林的「袋外得分」。

examples.en: We compared the out-of-bag score with performance on a separate set of examples from another garden.
examples.zh: 我们把「袋外得分」与模型在另一个花园的独立样本集上的表现作了比较。

collocations: compare the out-of-bag score with held-out performance

words.enDefinition: An uneven distribution of the number of observations across classes.

examples.en: We noticed class imbalance because the library sample contained many more novels than books of poetry.
examples.zh: 我们注意到「类别不平衡」，因为图书馆样本中的小说远多于诗集。

examples.en: The tutor discussed class imbalance before asking us which evaluation measure would capture the classifier's errors.
examples.zh: 老师先讨论了「类别不平衡」，再问哪个评估指标能反映分类器的错误。

words.enDefinition: The category with the most observations in the data being considered.

examples.en: Novels formed the majority class because they accounted for most of the examples in our exercise.
examples.zh: 小说是「多数类」，因为它们在练习中占样本的大部分。

examples.en: The simple baseline predicted the majority class for every book in the sample catalogue.
examples.zh: 简单的基准模型把示例目录中的每本书都预测为「多数类」。

collocations: count examples in the majority class
predict the majority class as a baseline

words.enDefinition: A category with relatively few examples in an imbalanced dataset.

examples.en: Poetry formed the minority class because only a few books in the sample carried that label.
examples.zh: 诗歌是「少数类」，因为样本里只有几本书带有该标签。

examples.en: We reported errors for the minority class separately after noticing how rarely those books appeared.
examples.zh: 发现这类书很少出现后，我们单独报告了「少数类」的错误。

collocations: evaluate recall for the minority class
count examples from the minority class

words.enDefinition: Increasing the number of training examples from a class by randomly drawing existing examples again.

examples.en: The exercise used random oversampling to give poetry examples more representation in the training portion.
examples.zh: 练习用「随机过采样」增加诗歌样本在训练部分中的占比。

examples.en: Our tutor applied random oversampling only after separating the training examples from the reserved ones.
examples.zh: 老师先把训练样本和留出样本分开，才应用「随机过采样」。

collocations: apply random oversampling to training data
use random oversampling for a rare class

words.enDefinition: Reducing a class's training examples by selecting a random subset to keep.

examples.en: We used random undersampling to keep fewer common leaf examples while comparing the two training approaches.
examples.zh: 我们用「随机欠采样」减少常见叶片样本的保留数量，再比较两种训练方法。

examples.en: The worksheet recorded how many novel descriptions remained after random undersampling in the training data.
examples.zh: 练习表记录了训练数据经「随机欠采样」后还剩多少条小说描述。

collocations: compare before and after random undersampling
use random undersampling on the majority class

words.enDefinition: Giving examples from different target classes different weights during model fitting.

examples.en: The team tried class weighting so that errors on rare poetry examples contributed more during fitting.
examples.zh: 团队尝试「类别加权」，让少数诗歌样本上的错误在拟合时占更大权重。

examples.en: Our tutor compared class weighting with changing the number of examples from each category.
examples.zh: 老师对比了「类别加权」和调整各类别样本数量这两种做法。

collocations: fit a model using class weighting

words.enDefinition: A simple reference model used to judge whether a more elaborate method improves performance.

examples.en: The baseline model always predicted the average sorting time observed in the training records.
examples.zh: 「基准模型」一律预测训练记录中观察到的平均分拣时间。

examples.en: We evaluated a baseline model before deciding whether the more complicated classifier added any benefit.
examples.zh: 我们先评估一个「基准模型」，再判断更复杂的分类器是否带来了改善。

words.enDefinition: Choosing a modeling approach or fitted configuration based on a specified comparison procedure.

examples.en: We used validation results for model selection before evaluating the chosen approach on the test set.
examples.zh: 我们先依据验证结果进行「模型选择」，再在测试集上评估选定的方法。

examples.en: The tutor asked us to describe the model selection criteria used in the library classification exercise.
examples.zh: 老师让我们说明图书馆分类练习所采用的「模型选择」标准。

collocations: use validation data for model selection
keep test data separate from model selection

words.enDefinition: Comparing settings chosen outside fitting to find a configuration with better validation performance.

examples.en: We used hyperparameter tuning to compare several limits on the depth of the plant classification tree.
examples.zh: 我们用「超参数调优」对比了植物分类树的几种深度限制。

examples.en: The report recorded which settings were considered during hyperparameter tuning for the time prediction model.
examples.zh: 报告记录了用时预测模型在「超参数调优」期间考虑了哪些设置。

collocations: use validation data for hyperparameter tuning

words.enDefinition: Evaluating every combination of specified candidate settings in a finite search grid.

examples.en: Our grid search tried each combination of the two tree settings listed in the worksheet.
examples.zh: 我们的「网格搜索」尝试了练习表所列两项树设置的每一种组合。

examples.en: The tutor expanded the grid search after adding a new candidate for maximum tree depth.
examples.zh: 老师加入一个新的最大树深度候选值后，扩大了「网格搜索」范围。

collocations: define candidates for a grid search
compare models with a grid search

words.enDefinition: Evaluating configurations sampled at random from specified settings or distributions.

examples.en: We used random search to try a limited number of settings from a larger candidate space.
examples.zh: 我们用「随机搜索」从较大的候选空间里试验数量有限的设置。

examples.en: Our tutor used random search when checking every possible combination would take too long.
examples.zh: 逐一检查所有可能组合耗时太久，老师因此用了「随机搜索」。

collocations: set the budget for random search
compare random search with grid search

words.enDefinition: A performance measure calculated on examples reserved for development evaluation.

examples.en: The validation score improved after we reduced the number of leaves allowed in the decision tree.
examples.zh: 限制决策树的叶节点数量后，「验证得分」提高了。

examples.en: We checked the validation score before deciding which version to keep for the final exercise.
examples.zh: 决定保留哪个版本做最后练习之前，我们先查看了「验证得分」。

collocations: select a model by validation score

words.enDefinition: A performance score from cross-validation, often reported per fold or summarized across folds.

examples.en: Our report gave the mean cross-validation score along with the individual scores for each held-out fold.
examples.zh: 我们的报告给出了平均「交叉验证得分」，同时也列出各留出折的单独得分。

examples.en: We compared the cross-validation score of the forest with that of a simple reference model.
examples.zh: 我们将森林的「交叉验证得分」与一个简单的参照模型作了比较。

words.enDefinition: A defined numerical measure used to judge predictions or another model outcome.

examples.en: Our group chose an evaluation metric that expressed sorting time errors directly in minutes.
examples.zh: 我们组选了一个以分钟直接表示分拣用时误差的「评估指标」。

examples.en: The tutor asked why that evaluation metric was useful for comparing the two plant classifiers.
examples.zh: 老师问，为什么这个「评估指标」适合比较这两个植物分类器。

collocations: compare models using the same evaluation metric

words.enDefinition: To fit the chosen model again, often on all development data after its settings are selected.

examples.en: We decided to refit the model on all development records after selecting the tree settings.
examples.zh: 选定树的设置后，我们决定用所有开发数据「重新拟合模型」。

examples.en: The worksheet asked us to refit the model before measuring performance on the untouched test set.
examples.zh: 练习表要求我们先「重新拟合模型」，再在未使用的测试集上测量表现。

collocations: refit the model with the chosen settings
refit the model on all development data
refit the model before final testing

words.enDefinition: Predictions for each example made by a model fitted without that example's validation fold.

examples.en: We collected out-of-fold predictions so each leaf's predicted label came from a fit that excluded it.
examples.zh: 我们收集了「折外预测」，使每片叶子的预测标签都由未用到它的拟合模型给出。

examples.en: Our tutor compared the out-of-fold predictions with the fitted model's predictions on all training examples.
examples.zh: 老师把「折外预测」与拟合模型在全部训练样本上的预测作了比较。

collocations: inspect out-of-fold predictions for individual examples

words.enDefinition: A table counting how often each observed class is paired with each predicted class.

examples.en: The confusion matrix showed that the model often labelled poetry books as works of fiction.
examples.zh: 「混淆矩阵」显示，模型经常把诗集标为小说。

examples.en: We checked the row labels before interpreting the confusion matrix in the garden classification exercise.
examples.zh: 解读花园分类练习的「混淆矩阵」之前，我们先核对了行标签。

collocations: inspect errors in a confusion matrix

words.enDefinition: An observation that belongs to the positive class and is predicted as positive.

examples.en: The worksheet marked an oak leaf as a true positive when the classifier correctly found it.
examples.zh: 分类器正确识别出一片橡树叶时，练习表将它记作「真正例」。

examples.en: We checked the recorded label before counting the photographed leaf as a true positive.
examples.zh: 把照片中的叶片计为「真正例」之前，我们先核对了记录的标签。

collocations: identify a true positive in the confusion matrix

words.enDefinition: An observation that belongs to the negative class and is predicted as negative.

examples.en: The classifier's correct rejection of a maple leaf counted as a true negative in the example.
examples.zh: 分类器正确排除了一片枫叶，因此在例题中算作「真负例」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked which row and column showed a true negative in the two-class matrix.
examples.zh: 老师问，二分类矩阵的哪一行哪一列显示「真负例」。

collocations: identify a true negative in the confusion matrix

words.enDefinition: The proportion of evaluated examples assigned the correct class in a single-label task.

examples.en: The team calculated classification accuracy by dividing the number of correctly labelled books by the total evaluated.
examples.zh: 团队用正确归类的图书数除以评估图书总数，计算「分类准确率」。

examples.en: We compared classification accuracy on the reserved garden photographs after choosing the final classifier.
examples.zh: 选定最终分类器后，我们比较了留出的花园照片上的「分类准确率」。

words.enDefinition: The unweighted average of per-class recall scores used to evaluate classification.

examples.en: The team reported balanced accuracy because one plant species was far more common than the others.
examples.zh: 因为一个植物物种远比其他物种常见，团队报告了「平衡准确率」。

examples.en: Our tutor calculated balanced accuracy after examining how well the classifier recovered each separate class.
examples.zh: 老师查看分类器识别各类别样本的表现后，计算了「平衡准确率」。

collocations: report balanced accuracy for imbalanced data

words.enDefinition: Among examples predicted as a given class, the proportion that actually belong to that class.

examples.en: The precision score fell because many books flagged as poetry were actually other kinds of writing.
examples.zh: 不少被标为诗歌的图书实际上是其他文体，因此「精确率」下降。

examples.en: Our tutor calculated the precision score using only the books the classifier had labelled as poetry.
examples.zh: 老师只用分类器标为诗歌的图书计算「精确率」。

collocations: compare a precision score with recall

words.enDefinition: Among examples that truly belong to a given class, the proportion successfully identified as that class.

examples.en: The recall score was low because the classifier missed many of the actual oak leaves.
examples.zh: 分类器漏掉了许多真正的橡树叶，因此「召回率」很低。

examples.en: We calculated the recall score from all the books that the librarian had marked as poetry.
examples.zh: 我们依据馆员标为诗歌的全部图书计算「召回率」。

words.enDefinition: The proportion of actual negative examples correctly predicted as negative.

examples.en: The tutor calculated specificity using only leaves that were not oak leaves in the test sample.
examples.zh: 老师仅根据测试样本里的非橡树叶计算「特异度」。

examples.en: The worksheet showed higher specificity when fewer non-oak leaves were incorrectly flagged as oak leaves.
examples.zh: 错误标为橡树叶的非橡树叶变少时，练习表显示「特异度」提升了。

words.enDefinition: The proportion of actual negative examples incorrectly predicted as positive.

examples.en: The false positive rate increased when more non-oak leaves were incorrectly classified as oak leaves.
examples.zh: 更多非橡树叶被错分为橡树叶时，「假正率」上升了。

examples.en: We compared the false positive rate at two probability thresholds in the plant exercise.
examples.zh: 在植物练习中，我们比较了两个概率阈值下的「假正率」。

collocations: compare the false positive rate across thresholds

words.enDefinition: The proportion of actual positive examples incorrectly predicted as negative.

examples.en: The false negative rate was higher for the model that missed more of the actual oak leaves.
examples.zh: 漏掉更多真正橡树叶的模型，其「假负率」更高。

examples.en: Our tutor asked which denominator was needed to calculate the false negative rate for poetry detection.
examples.zh: 老师问，计算诗歌识别的「假负率」要用哪个分母。

collocations: compare false negative rates across models

words.enDefinition: For a given class, the harmonic mean of precision and recall.

examples.en: The class used the F1 score because it wanted to consider both precision and recall.
examples.zh: 全班使用「F1 分数」，因为希望同时考察精确率与召回率。

examples.en: We compared the F1 score for poetry with the score for a more common category.
examples.zh: 我们把诗歌的「F1 分数」与另一个更常见类别的得分作了比较。

collocations: report the F1 score for a class

words.enDefinition: A mean of per-class scores that gives each class equal weight.

examples.en: We used a macro average so every book category counted equally in the reported F1 value.
examples.zh: 我们用「宏平均」，让图书的各类别在报告的 F1 值中权重相同。

examples.en: The tutor explained why the macro average fell after the classifier missed a rare plant species.
examples.zh: 老师解释了为什么分类器漏掉一种稀少的植物后，「宏平均」下降了。

collocations: compare a macro average with a weighted average

words.enDefinition: A score computed by pooling the underlying classification counts across classes before applying the metric.

examples.en: We obtained the micro average by combining the classification counts before calculating the final precision score.
examples.zh: 我们先汇总分类计数，再计算最终精确率，得到「微平均」。

examples.en: The report gave a micro average for the book labels along with a score for each class.
examples.zh: 报告给出了图书标签的「微平均」，并列出了各类别的得分。

collocations: compare a micro average with per-class scores

words.zhGloss: 按类样本数加权的平均值
words.enDefinition: An average of per-class scores weighted by the numbers of actual examples in those classes.
acceptedZhAnswers: 按类样本数加权的平均值

examples.en: The support-weighted average gave the common novel category more influence than the smaller poetry category.
examples.zh: 「按类样本数加权的平均值」让常见的小说类比数量较少的诗歌类产生更大的影响。

examples.en: Our tutor checked the class counts before calculating the support-weighted average for the exercise.
examples.zh: 老师先核对各类别样本数，再计算练习中「按类样本数加权的平均值」。

collocations: compare the support-weighted average with the macro average

words.enDefinition: a plot with false positive rate on the horizontal axis and true positive rate on the vertical axis across thresholds

examples.en: The ROC curve showed how correct detections and false alarms changed as we moved the threshold.
examples.zh: 「ROC 曲线」展示了我们改变阈值时正确识别率和误报率如何变化。

examples.en: Our tutor checked the axes before comparing the ROC curve for each of the leaf classifiers.
examples.zh: 对比各叶片分类器的「ROC 曲线」之前，老师先核对了坐标轴。

collocations: choose a point on an ROC curve

words.enDefinition: The area under the ROC curve, summarizing how well scores separate positives from negatives across thresholds.

examples.en: We compared ROC AUC to judge how well each model ranked oak leaves above other leaves.
examples.zh: 我们对比了「ROC 曲线下面积」，判断各模型将橡树叶排在其他叶片之前的能力。

examples.en: The tutor reported ROC AUC separately from accuracy at the single threshold chosen for classification.
examples.zh: 老师将「ROC 曲线下面积」与分类所选单一阈值下的准确率分开报告。

collocations: report ROC AUC on held-out examples

words.enDefinition: A plot showing precision and recall at different classification thresholds.

examples.en: The precision-recall curve showed what happened to precision when the classifier found more poetry books.
examples.zh: 「精确率—召回率曲线」展示了分类器找出更多诗歌书籍时精确率如何变化。

examples.en: We used the precision-recall curve to examine different thresholds for finding the rarer plant species.
examples.zh: 我们用「精确率—召回率曲线」考察检测较少见植物物种的不同阈值。

collocations: choose a point on the precision-recall curve

words.enDefinition: A weighted sum of precision values across thresholds, with weights given by successive increases in recall.

examples.en: We compared average precision for the two classifiers that ranked books by their likelihood of being poetry.
examples.zh: 我们比较了两个分类器的「平均精确率」，它们都按属于诗歌的可能性给图书排序。

examples.en: The tutor explained how changes in recall affect the weighting used to calculate average precision.
examples.zh: 老师解释了召回率的变化怎样影响计算「平均精确率」时的权重。

words.enDefinition: The average negative logarithm of the probability assigned to the class that actually occurred.

examples.en: The classifier received a larger log loss after assigning a very low probability to the correct label.
examples.zh: 分类器给正确标签分配的概率很低，因而「对数损失」更大。

examples.en: We used log loss to compare the two models that returned probabilities for each plant class.
examples.zh: 我们用「对数损失」比较两个会为各植物类别返回概率的模型。

collocations: penalize confident errors with log loss

words.enDefinition: For a binary outcome, the mean squared difference between its predicted probability and its zero-or-one outcome.

examples.en: We calculated the Brier score using predicted oak probabilities and the actual labels for the photographed leaves.
examples.zh: 我们用照片中叶片的橡树叶预测概率和实际标签计算「布里尔分数」。

examples.en: The tutor compared the Brier score before and after revising the probabilities in the example.
examples.zh: 老师比较了更改例题中概率之前和之后的「布里尔分数」。

collocations: report the Brier score for probability predictions

words.enDefinition: The average absolute difference between numerical predictions and their observed values.

examples.en: The mean absolute error showed the typical size of the sorting time errors in minutes.
examples.zh: 「平均绝对误差」用分钟表示分拣用时预测的平均误差幅度。

examples.en: We calculated mean absolute error after converting the predictions and observations to the same unit.
examples.zh: 把预测值和观测值换成同一种单位后，我们计算了「平均绝对误差」。

collocations: compare mean absolute error across models
report mean absolute error in original units

words.enDefinition: The arithmetic mean of the squared differences between numerical predictions and observations.

examples.en: The mean squared error rose sharply when one predicted sorting time was far from its observed value.
examples.zh: 某次分拣时间的预测值与观测值相差很大时，「均方误差」显著上升。

examples.en: We used mean squared error to compare time models while emphasizing larger mistakes in the classroom results.
examples.zh: 我们用「均方误差」比较用时模型，着重反映课堂结果中幅度较大的错误。

collocations: compare mean squared error across models

words.enDefinition: The square root of the mean squared error, expressed in the target's original units.

examples.en: The root mean squared error was reported in minutes for every model in the workshop comparison.
examples.zh: 工作坊比较中的所有模型都以分钟报告「均方根误差」。

examples.en: Our tutor computed root mean squared error after squaring the prediction errors and averaging those squares.
examples.zh: 老师先对各个预测误差平方并求平均，再计算「均方根误差」。

collocations: compare root mean squared error across models
report root mean squared error in minutes

words.enDefinition: The middle value of the absolute errors across examples, using the median convention.

examples.en: The class calculated median absolute error to describe a typical mistake despite one very unusual sorting time.
examples.zh: 尽管有一次分拣用时非常异常，大家还是用「绝对误差中位数」描述典型误差。

examples.en: We compared median absolute error across the models using the same set of recorded completion times.
examples.zh: 我们依据同一组已记录的完成用时比较各模型的「绝对误差中位数」。

collocations: compare median absolute error with the mean

words.enDefinition: one minus the ratio of squared prediction error to squared deviation from the observed mean, when the observed target varies

examples.en: The R-squared score was negative when the predictions were worse than using the observed mean.
examples.zh: 预测结果还不如直接用观测均值时，「决定系数」为负。

examples.en: Our tutor checked the R-squared score against the error in minutes reported for the same model.
examples.zh: 老师把「决定系数」与同一模型按分钟报告的误差作了对照。

collocations: report the R-squared score on test data

words.enDefinition: a per-observation score comparing its mean distance to its own cluster with the smallest mean distance to another cluster

examples.en: The leaf had a negative silhouette coefficient because it was closer on average to the other group.
examples.zh: 这片叶子平均而言更接近另一组，因此它的「单样本轮廓系数」为负。

examples.en: We checked the silhouette coefficient for the book description positioned between two groups in the exercise.
examples.zh: 我们检查了练习中位于两组之间的图书描述的「单样本轮廓系数」。

words.enDefinition: The mean of the per-example silhouette coefficients for a clustering result.

examples.en: The silhouette score helped us compare two possible groupings of the same set of leaf measurements.
examples.zh: 「平均轮廓系数」帮助我们比较同一组叶片测量值的两种可能分组。

examples.en: Our tutor reported the silhouette score alongside individual scores for observations lying near group boundaries.
examples.zh: 老师报告了「平均轮廓系数」，同时列出了靠近分组边界的观测值的单独得分。

words.enDefinition: A comparison of two clusterings based on pairs of observations, adjusted for agreement expected by chance.

examples.en: We calculated the adjusted Rand index to compare our two groupings of the same book descriptions.
examples.zh: 我们计算了「调整兰德指数」，以比较同一批图书描述的两种分组方式。

examples.en: Our tutor used the adjusted Rand index after matching the rows shared by both sets of assignments.
examples.zh: 老师先匹配两组分配结果共有的观测行，然后使用「调整兰德指数」。

collocations: compare cluster assignments using the adjusted Rand index

words.enDefinition: In k-means, the sum of squared distances from observations to their assigned cluster centers.

examples.en: Cluster inertia was lower when the new centers lay closer to the leaves assigned to them.
examples.zh: 新中心更靠近分给它们的叶片时，「聚类惯性」较低。

examples.en: We compared cluster inertia across several fits with the same number of clusters and features.
examples.zh: 我们比较了簇数和特征数相同的几次拟合的「聚类惯性」。

words.enDefinition: A plot comparing predicted probabilities with observed event frequencies across groups of predictions.

examples.en: The calibration curve compared mean predicted probabilities with the observed share of oak leaves in each bin.
examples.zh: 「校准曲线」比较各分箱的平均预测概率与实际橡树叶所占比例。

examples.en: We checked the calibration curve to see whether the observed frequencies tracked the estimated probabilities.
examples.zh: 我们查看了「校准曲线」，确认观测频率是否和估计概率吻合。

collocations: compare a calibration curve with the diagonal

words.enDefinition: one minus the ratio of prediction-error variance to target variance when the observed numerical target has nonzero variance

examples.en: Our tutor compared the explained variance score with R-squared after adding a constant to the predictions.
examples.zh: 老师给预测值统一加上一个常数后，比较了「解释方差得分」与决定系数。

examples.en: The worksheet used the explained variance score to describe how well predictions tracked changes in sorting times.
examples.zh: 练习表用「解释方差得分」描述预测结果在多大程度上跟随分拣时间的变化。

collocations: compare the explained variance score with R-squared
